title: A live run by a Mind, through Telegram
label: live · paid · testnet (Sepolia test USDC)
source: Mind reply on Telegram, screen recording refs/telegram-ask.mp4 (bubble stamped 21:14 local). Question: "Should we hash or curtail tonight?"

hours.note: provisional: no 15-minute interval of the hour was published yet

receipts.detail: $26.36/PH/day = 46,755.12 sats/PH-day at block 976849. Public mempool.space said $26.54/PH/day (BTC $56,377, 965 EH/s).
$2.11/MWh. Matches public ERCOT MIS NP6-905-CD. Provisional.
7 answers at $0.01 each. Each matched ERCOT MIS NP4-190-CD to the cent.
Accepted max 21.5 C. Public Open-Meteo archive said 22.8 C.

receiptsNote: Receipt ids are as listed in the Mind's reply and shortened there. The weather receipt is not on the record I have, so none is shown.

holds.intro: Two earlier runs ended in HOLD instead of a guess (Mind replies 06a48c8e23 and 055fe017b0). Their causes, and what changed:

items.detail: The hashprice ask went through the Anjoman API route, and answers attributed to Gauge came back all null while Gauge itself answered the same blocks correctly.
items.fix: Hashprice is now bought on the escrow route from the named miner.

items.detail: The forecast fetch failed, so that check was missing and Ballast said so instead of guessing.
items.fix: A weather forecast fallback, and restated hashprice answers are read.

items.detail: The Anjoman API treats a named miner as a hint, and its ranking sent ERCOT HB_WEST asks to NYISO providers.
items.fix: Power prices are bought on the escrow route straight from the named miner.

mismatch.problem: Hashprice disagreed with the public reference
mismatch.detail: Traced to the hashrate basis: 965.1 vs 1,026.4 EH/s. The gap fell from 7.6% to 1.3%.

notes: Pecos is our own miner, so this is an internal test, not outside usage.
Ballast recommends only. No miner was switched.
